summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, morbid obesity, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement was admitted for worsening left leg pain, swelling, and erythema following trauma to the shin. She was treated initially with IV vancomycin for suspected cellulitis, but due to difficulty maintaining therapeutic levels, was transitioned to oral linezolid. Wound culture showed no growth, but clinical improvement was observed. Her heart failure was stable on home diuretics, and anticoagulation with warfarin was carefully monitored. She completed a course of antibiotics, was deemed stable for discharge, and was sent home with home health services to continue wound care and medication management.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Heart valve replaced by other means
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
